title: 7-day dopamine reset
intro: A week to let your reward system recalibrate. Each day has a short read and one small action. Go at your own pace — a missed day is fine, just pick it back up.

days.title: Understand the reset
days.action: Name your three biggest sources of cheap, instant stimulation (e.g. endless scrolling, sugar, the behaviour itself).

blocks.text: A dopamine reset isn't about having zero pleasure. It's about turning down the flood of cheap, instant hits so that ordinary, effortful rewards start to feel good again.
When everything is one tap away, the brain's baseline rises and real life feels flat by comparison. Over a week of dialing down the easy hits, that baseline starts to drop back to normal.
The goal this week: fewer cheap hits, more slow rewards. That's the whole reset in one line.

days.title: Turn down the novelty
days.action: Pick one high-novelty feed (social media, news, shorts) and take a full day off it.

blocks.text: Endless novelty — new post, new video, new tab — is one of the strongest drivers of the wanting system. It trains your brain to expect a fresh hit every few seconds.
Today, remove one source of that novelty for the whole day. Notice the pull to check it. That pull is exactly what you're retraining.

days.title: Boredom is the point
days.action: Sit with 10 minutes of doing nothing — no phone, no screen. Just be bored.

blocks.text: We reach for stimulation the instant boredom appears. But boredom isn't an emergency — it's the empty space where your mind resets and creativity returns.
Let yourself be bored on purpose today. It's uncomfortable for about 90 seconds, and then it isn't.

days.title: Choose a slow reward
days.action: Do one thing that's rewarding but effortful: cook a real meal, read a chapter, finish a small project.

blocks.text: Slow rewards — the kind that take effort and time — are where lasting satisfaction lives. They don't spike dopamine; they build it steadily and leave you feeling good, not empty.
Pick one today. Notice that the satisfaction lands after the effort, not before. That's the opposite of the loop.

days.title: Move your body
days.action: Get 20 minutes of movement — a walk, a run, a workout. Anything that raises your heart rate.

blocks.text: Exercise is one of the most reliable ways to reset mood and reward chemistry naturally. It also discharges the restless energy that urges ride on.
You don't need a perfect workout. Twenty minutes of moving is enough to shift your state for hours.

days.title: Reach for connection
days.action: Have one real conversation — in person or by call, not text.

blocks.text: Connection is a deep, slow reward the loop can never replace. Isolation feeds compulsion; contact starves it.
Reach out to one person today. You don't need a reason beyond wanting to.

days.title: Reflect and keep what worked
days.action: Write down one thing that felt different this week, and one small rule you'll keep going.

blocks.text: A week isn't a finish line — it's a recalibration. Notice what shifted: sleep, mood, the strength of urges, how ordinary things felt.
Now choose one small, sustainable rule to carry forward. Not ten. One you'll actually keep.
The reset works because you proved to yourself that the cheap hits weren't giving you much. That knowledge is yours now.
